newsitem.title: GERMANY: Man who dissolved East German Stasi was informer.
newsitem.headline: Man who dissolved East German Stasi was informer.

text.p: The man East Germany's last communist government named to dissolve its hated Stasi security apparatus turns out to have been a Stasi informer himself, the chairman of a parliamentary committee said on Friday.

Guenter Eichhorn, who is being questioned by a committee investigating Ministry for State Security (Stasi) activities, was confronted on Thursday with documents he had signed in 1970 and 1985 agreeing to work as an informer.
He admitted he had informed for the secret police under the code name "Adler" (Eagle), despite having previously denied any links with the organisation, Volker Neumann told German Radio.
Eichhorn was put in charge of disbanding the Stasi in February 1990 when East Germany's last communist leader, Hans Modrow, was forced to agree to dismantle the security apparatus.
Modrow had been under pressure to dissolve the Stasi from late November 1989, after the collapse of the Berlin Wall and East Berlin's hardline communist government.
But he first changed its name to the Office for National Security, saying East Germany had to have some kind of security apparatus.
It took until February 8, 1990 for Modrow to agree to dismantle the Stasi systematically, after which Eichhorn was appointed to do the job.
Experts say key Stasi files continued to be destroyed at least until the first democratic election in East Germany on March 18 of the same year.
The committee heard that Eichhorn held meetings with Stasi officers in his flat, and that a four cm-thick file exists with information on his contacts with Stasi representatives.
